uncited: The A-buffer sampling method maps scattered input data points onto a rectangular grid by accumulating weighted contributions from all nearby points, rather than selecting a single nearest neighbor.
It solves the problem of converting unstructured point cloud data into a structured voxel grid suitable for volume rendering.

It differs from its sibling [Z-buffer Sampling Method](5425-z-buffer-sampling-method.md) by preserving data accuracy through weighted averaging instead of nearest-neighbor assignment, producing more accurate images at the cost of higher computational time.
**Inputs:** A set of scattered input data points (each with coordinates and a scalar value) and a target rectangular grid defined by its cell dimensions.
**Outputs:** A rectangular grid where each node contains an interpolated scalar value derived from the input points.
The implementation requires a grid data structure.

*Edge Case:* If `accumulated_weight` is 0 (no points contributed), the node remains undefined or empty.
A nearest-neighbor sampling technique that assigns data values to grid nodes based on minimum distance, analogous to hidden-surface removal in rasterization.
It differs from the A-buffer method by performing a single closest-point assignment per node rather than accumulating weighted contributions.
It is chosen when execution speed is prioritized over accuracy, or for preliminary visual analysis to determine optimal grid resolution.
**Time Complexity:** The A-buffer method requires iterating over all grid nodes for each input point (or vice versa with spatial indexing), leading to higher computational cost.
**Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for two accumulators (value and weight) per grid node, plus the input point data.
**Strengths:** Preserves data structure and smoothness; handles overlapping contributions from multiple points naturally.
**When to use:** When high accuracy is required for volume visualization and computational resources allow.
It was adapted for volume visualization to map scattered data onto rectangular grids.
The report compares it against a Z-buffer method and notes its superiority in image accuracy.
